title: IVF Paperwork, Marriage Certificate & Legal Rules in Türkiye Explained

metaDescription: Marriage certificate Apostille rules, donor prohibitions, pre-arrival labs, and fertility medication customs rules for foreign IVF couples in Türkiye.
quickAnswer: Foreign couples seeking IVF in Türkiye must be legally married, use only their own eggs and sperm, and present a valid marriage certificate—often Apostilled and translated into Turkish by a sworn translator—before stimulation begins. Egg donation, sperm donation, embryo donation, and surrogacy are strictly prohibited under Turkish Ministry of Health regulations.

What exact marriage documentation and Apostille/translation rules apply to foreign IVF couples?

Under Turkish assisted reproduction rules, clinics may treat only legally married heterosexual couples using their own gametes, and both spouses must sign separate written consent forms before procedures start. Foreign couples generally need their original civil marriage certificate, valid passports, and, where requested by the licensed center, an Apostille plus notarized Turkish translation.

The legal framework stems from the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health Assisted Reproductive Treatment Regulation](https://saglik.gov.tr/TR-10515/uremeye-yardimci-tedavi-uygulamalari-ve-uremeye-yardimci-tedavi-merkezleri-hakkinda-yonetmelik.html) (Official Gazette No. 29135). Because clinics face strict Ministry inspections, front-desk teams cannot waive civil status verification.

If your marriage certificate was issued in a member state of the [HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41), obtain an Apostille from your home country's designated authority before flying. Türkiye has been a party to the convention since 1985, and its competent authorities are listed through the [HCCH Türkiye Authority Directory](https://www.hcch.net/en/states/authorities/details3/?aid=350). Couples from non-Apostille countries typically need consular legalization from the Turkish embassy or consulate in the issuing country. Once in Istanbul, a sworn translator (yeminli tercüman) and Turkish notary (noter) handle the Turkish certification if your hospital requires local notarization.

body.text: Why are egg donation, sperm donation and surrogacy illegal in Türkiye?

Egg donation, sperm donation, embryo donation, and surrogacy are illegal in Türkiye because national health legislation restricts assisted reproductive treatment to a married couple's own biological gametes. Turkish authorities enforce this rule to maintain direct genetic traceability and prohibit third-party reproduction across all licensed public and private fertility centers.

The prohibition applies across the entire country without exceptions for foreign nationals, as established under the [Ministry of Health Assisted Reproductive Treatment Regulation](https://saglik.gov.tr/TR-10515/uremeye-yardimci-tedavi-uygulamalari-ve-uremeye-yardimci-tedavi-merkezleri-hakkinda-yonetmelik.html). Sex selection is likewise restricted solely to preventing severe sex-linked genetic disorders. Couples can verify that a hospital holds active authorization to treat international patients through the [Ministry of Health Health Tourism Department](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html). Because we operate independently of clinic commissions, [our two-founder team](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) never steers couples toward unlicensed workarounds or cross-border referrals.
What lab tests can be done at home before Day 2 of your cycle?

Completing baseline hormone panels, infectious disease screening, and semen analysis at home before Cycle Day 2 can shorten your stay in Türkiye and flag protocol adjustments early. However, many Turkish fertility centers still require local infectious disease re-testing under Turkish laboratory accreditation rules before egg retrieval or embryo freezing.

Doing preliminary diagnostics locally helps your treating specialist evaluate ovarian reserve and stimulation dosing before you book non-refundable flights. Review this pre-departure paperwork checklist with your physician:

items: Female baseline bloodwork: AMH, Day 2–3 FSH, LH, Estradiol (E2), Prolactin, TSH, Free T4, and complete blood count.
Male partner workup: Recent semen analysis (within 3–6 months) following your clinic's abstinence window.
Infectious disease panel (both spouses): HIV, Hepatitis B (HBsAg), Hepatitis C (Anti-HCV), and VDRL/syphilis screening, noting that clinics may repeat these locally.
Imaging and prior history: Transvaginal ultrasound notes, HSG reports, and summaries of any earlier stimulation cycles or surgeries.
Translated summaries: English or Turkish lab printouts showing clear reference ranges and test dates.

How do medication customs rules work for fertility injections?

Travellers entering Türkiye may carry reasonable personal-use quantities of prescription fertility injections in hand luggage, provided they bring a signed physician's prescription or medical report confirming personal treatment during the trip. Keep all pens, vials, and needles in original pharmacy packaging with matching patient names for customs inspection.

Under the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Trade Passenger Transactions Guide](https://ticaret.gov.tr/gumruk-islemleri/sikca-sorulan-sorular/english/passenger-transactions), personal prescription medicines are permitted when supported by a prescription or physician's document stating the traveller must use them during travel. General border entry guidance is also published by the [Ministry of Foreign Affairs](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/turkiye_ye-ait-gumruk-bilgileri.en.mfa). Pack temperature-sensitive gonadotropins in an insulated medical cooler with gel packs approved by your airline, carry a separate sharps/needle letter for airport security, and confirm whether your Turkish treating team prefers you to purchase stimulation medications locally at licensed Turkish pharmacies after your Day 2 scan.

faq.q: Can unmarried couples or single women undergo IVF in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Turkish law restricts assisted reproductive treatment to legally married heterosexual couples using their own eggs and sperm. Clinics verify civil marriage records and both spouses' passports before starting treatment.

faq.q: Does an electronic Apostille (e-Apostille) work in Türkiye?
faq.a: Türkiye participates in the Hague Apostille Convention and recognizes valid Apostilles from convention member states, though individual clinics and notaries may request a printed verifiable copy for their physical patient archive. Confirm the format with your hospital coordinator before departure.

faq.q: How long should foreign couples plan to stay in Istanbul for a full IVF cycle?
faq.a: Most couples doing a fresh stimulation cycle from Cycle Day 2 through embryo transfer plan for roughly 16 to 20 days, while those splitting stimulation and a frozen transfer often stay 12 to 14 days on the first visit. Your licensed medical team sets the exact clinical timeline.

faq.q: Can frozen embryos be shipped out of Türkiye to another country?
faq.a: Turkish regulations outline domestic transfers between licensed Turkish centers rather than a routine pathway for international embryo export. Plan on returning to Türkiye for frozen transfers unless competent Turkish authorities confirm another route in writing.

faq.q: Are fertility medications cheaper to buy in Türkiye than bringing them from home?
faq.a: Many patients purchase stimulation pens locally at licensed Turkish pharmacies using a Turkish physician's prescription, as local retail prices are regulated. Always ask your treating doctor which option fits your protocol before flying.
